Union Territory Of J And K And Ors Through: Mr. Mohsin Qadri, Sr. Aag Mr. Bikramdeep Singh, Dy. Ag Mr. Hakim Aman Ali, Dy. Ag Mr. Waseem Gul, Ga Coram: Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnesh Oswal, Judge Order
texts.facts: However, learned counsel for the parties submit that considering the issue that requires consideration by this Court, Commissioner, Food Safety and Controller, Drugs and Food Control Organisation, UT of Jammu and Kashmir, Srinagar/ Jammu, would be the necessary party. Therefore, on their oral prayer, Commissioner, Food Safety and Controller, Drugs and Food Control Organisation, UT of Jammu and Kashmir, Srinagar/ Jammu, is arrayed as respondent no.6. Registry to update the cause title of the petition. Accordingly, Mr. Hakim Aman Ali, Dy.AG, accepts notice on behalf of respondent no.6. Response/ objections, if any, on behalf of the respondents be filed before the adjourned date failing which appropriate orders shall follow.
texts.arguments: "Mr. Mir Umar, a practicing lawyer, has petitioned this Court in public interest to highlight the unchecked sale of rotten, unhygienic and unsafe meat and poultry products in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in the meanwhile he shall also place on record the additional material that is germane to the matter in issue". Response on behalf of respondents 3 and 6 has been submitted. But despite the matter being sensitive, the Municipal Corporation(s), Jammu as also Srinagar have chosen to remain silent. Thus render no assistance. Learned Amicus Curiae submits that immediate judicial intervention is warranted to address grave public health crisis in the J&K, particularly Kashmir valley, that stems from large scale sale of rotten, unhygienic meat, fish and poultry products. With reference to several reports published in leading newspapers and aired on television channels, he asserts that such meat and poultry is transported into J&K from different parts of the country in unhygienic conditions. Without cold-chain facilities and requisite certification by authorized veterinary officers. Thus, he submits, the apparent inaction and indifference on part of the concerned authorities including the Directorate of Food Safety, the Municipal Corporation(s), the Health Department as also the law enforcement agencies to curb this menace, demonstrate gross administrative negligence and apathy. Something that is in violation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as also the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011. Further, the Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Corporation Act, 2000, mandates regulation, licensing, and inspection of slaughterhouses, meat markets as also the premises where food is processed or sold. But apparently the authorities have failed to discharge their statutory duties/obligations. Therefore, it is urged that recent discovery of large quantity of rotten meat in Kashmir has rather Mir Umar vs Union Territory Of J And K And Ors on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149837969/ 2 underscore the immediate need for strict regulatory mechanism. He submits that the individuals who were earlier involved in the trade of rotten meat have now diverted their business activities towards supply and sale of synthethic/adulterated cheese, which poses equally serious and adverse health hazards. With reference to a column (Annexure I) in one of the local newspapers, he submits that following an intel from Government Railway Police (GRP) Jammu regarding the arrival of a suspicious consignment of cheese from Ambala, the Food Safety Wing of the Drug and Food Control Organization, J&K seized a huge consignment of 2100 kg (21 quintals) of adulterated 'Cheese' belonging to Shri Balaji Trading Company. Additionally, 78 tins of Trishool Brand Mustard Oil that had expired in 2023, were also seized. Accordingly, it is urged that public interest impels that the scope of this petition be further broadened. In response, Mr. Mohsin Qadri, learned senior counsel for the respondents, as always, fairly submits that the matter at hand is not adversarial in nature and is being pursued in the right earnest for public good.
